detail: Newell suffered the toe injury in the Nov. 4 win over Washington and is now set to miss an extended period. With Mouhamed Gueye (foot) expected to miss at least three more weeks, Aaron Wiggins and Corey Kispert could see a slight bump in minutes moving forward.

Veesaar suffered the injury during a workout on Sept. 15, and an MRI confirmed the diagnosis. The No. 52 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Veesaar was expected to spend a lot of time with Atlanta's G League affiliate this season.

Robinson will miss both halves of this back-to-back set due to an illness. The big man's next opportunity to play will come Tuesday at Washington. Luka Garza will likely see increased minutes in Robinson's stead.

George will sit out the second leg of this back-to-back set. With the veteran forward sidelined, Baylor Scheierman, Hugo Gonzalez and Sam Hauser could all see increased burn. George will likely return for Tuesday's game at Washington.

Williams started in Tuesday's 118-114 loss to the Lakers, but he will sit out Friday to rest. With Grayson Allen (concussion) also sidelined, Royce O'Neale could find his way into the starting lineup.

Allen is currently dealing with concussion-like symptoms and is in line for a second straight absence. Sion James and Royce O'Neale should continue to see an uptick in playing time until Allen is cleared to return.

Claxton will miss Sunday's contest due to an illness. He started Friday's 98-94 loss to the Wizards with Jalen Smith (illness) sidelined, but the latter is expected to return versus Denver. Zach Collins and Noa Essengue should get a bump in opportunities with Claxton out.

Smith was initially listed as questionable but is now expected to return from a one-game absence due to an illness. Over his last five appearances, the big man has averaged 17.2 points, 8.2 rebounds, 2.8 assists, 1.2 steals and 1.2 blocks across 28.2 minutes per showing. He could also see a slight bump in minutes if Nic Claxton (illness) is ruled out.
Williams is dealing with a sprained thumb on his non-shooting hand, but he's expected to play through it. Williams is averaging 6.9 points and 1.9 assists per game this season.

The rookie forward went down during Wednesday's loss to the Spurs, and he now needs surgery to repair a fractured right hand. More pressure will likely fall on Josh Giddey going forward, while the likes of Tre Jones and Isaac Okoro will have a chance for added streaming value.

Tyson will miss a third consecutive contest due to a right ankle injury, and his next chance to play will come Monday at Chicago. With Evan Mobley (toe) out and Peyton Watson (back) questionable, Tyrese Proctor, Meleek Thomas and Mario Hezonja could all see increased playing time once again.

Tomlin, who is recovering from a lower back stress reaction, has yet to suit up for the Cavs this season. He continues to get ruled out 24 hours in advance of tipoff, indicating he's still not close, so he can be viewed as week-to-week moving forward.

Washington is in danger of missing a second straight contest due to an illness. Zaccharie Risacher started in place of Washington during Saturday's 110-100 win over the Clippers, and that is likely to be the case again versus Utah.

Lawal will miss a third consecutive game due to a right groin strain. His absence won't have much of an impact on the Mavericks' rotation. Lawal's next chance to suit up will come Tuesday against Denver.

Curry suffered the injury early during Wednesday's loss to the Rockets, with head coach Steve Kerr saying after the game that the superstar point guard "tweaked" something in his abdominal area. Curry has never dealt with an injury of this nature, so the Warriors, who are off to a hot start spearheaded by Rookie of the Year candidate Yaxel Lendeborg, will likely proceed with caution. Brandin Podziemski, Brandon Williams (hamstring), De'Anthony Melton, Will Richard and Gary Payton (knee) are all candidates for increased roles until Curry is cleared to play again.

Porzingis said he was looking forward to joining the Warriors, but his body didn't respond the way he wanted it too during his ramp-up process before the season. Additionally, he said he will work with the Warriors on a solution that "makes sense." Porzingis is making this decision to prioritize his health and will hopefully turn a corner soon on that front.

McConnell missed the Pacers' first nine games of the 2026-27 campaign because of a right hamstring issue. However, he exited Friday's 128-119 loss to the Cavaliers due to left hamstring soreness. McConnell will have another opportunity to play Monday versus Oklahoma City, but for now, he should be considered day-to-day. In the meantime, Quenton Jackson is in line for more minutes behind Andrew Nembhard.

Sheppard required a full repair and is without a definitive timetable for a return to action. With Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) expected to miss at least two weeks, Quenton Jackson figures to see a significant uptick in playing time. Two-way player Braden Smith could also see increased action with the parent club.

It's unclear exactly what Small is dealing with, but for now, he can be considered questionable for Monday's meeting in Charlotte. With Small out, Cam Spencer and Jahmai Mashack will fill the minutes behind Ty Jerome.

The rookie sensation is sitting out for the first time this year and can be deemed day-to-day for the time being. His absence puts a ton of pressure on Ty Jerome (hip), who's set to return from a three-game layoff, and opens up a spot in the starting lineup likely for Isaiah Stewart.

Antetokounmpo previously dealt with a wrist injury in November, and he's now working through a groin issue that puts his status for Sunday's game up in the air. He has yet to miss a game this season, but if he's not cleared to play against Oklahoma City, then Andrew Wiggins and Bobby Portis would be the top candidates to enter Miami's starting lineup.

Murphy has missed seven of New Orleans' past eight games due to bilateral patellar tendinopathy, though he's expected to suit up Monday. The 26-year-old swingman logged 29 minutes off the bench in Friday's loss to the Thunder, marking his return after a six-game stint on the inactive list. He could remain restricted if he's cleared to play Monday.

This was the expectation after the star guard requested a trade from the Pelicans earlier Friday. Given his standing with the club, Murray can be tentatively considered doubtful for future contests while New Orleans tries to find him another home.

Towns missed Saturday's 97-96 win over Portland due to an illness, and that same ailment could force him to miss a second consecutive game. Andre Drummond got the start in Towns' place while James Wiseman saw a season-high 25 minutes off the bench. If Towns is forced to sit again Sunday, expect a similar approach for New York.

Once Sorber begins on-court work, there will be a ramp-up period before he's cleared for game-time action, so his absence will likely extend well beyond this initial 6-8-week window. Sorber was selected by the Thunder with the No. 15 pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, but he missed his entire rookie season after tearing the ACL in his right knee and has yet to play this season due to right knee issues.

This is another massive blow to an Oklahoma City squad that's already set to be without Jalen Williams (leg) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) for most, if not all, of the season. With Holmgren sidelined, Kenrich Williams, Jaylin Williams and Aday Mara are all candidates to see increased playing time. Two-way player Brooks Barnhizer could also see more minutes.

Dunn exited Friday's win over Utah early due to a right quad injury, though it's encouraging that he was able to practice Sunday. The Suns will provide an update on his status for Monday's game at New Orleans by Sunday night.

Krejci suffered the ankle injury in last Wednesday's win over the Suns and is set to miss an extended period after undergoing surgery. With the 26-year-old and Ja Morant (hamstring) both on the shelf, Jrue Holiday and Sidy Cissoko should continue seeing increased minutes.

Murray-Boyles exited Wednesday's game versus the Wizards and didn't suit up for Friday's 105-102 win over the Pistons. It appears a one-game absence will be all that is needed for the 21-year-old, though it's unclear if he will reclaim his spot in the starting lineup over Allen Graves.

Carrington was a late addition to the injury report due to an illness. If the third-year guard is unable to play Sunday, Tre Johnson could see a slight bump in minutes. Carrington has seen limited playing time of late, totaling just eight minutes in two appearances over Washington's last three games.

Ayton played 11 minutes during Friday's 98-94 win over Chicago, but he appears to have picked up some sort of illness over the weekend. If he can't play Sunday, expect Khris Middleton and Bilal Coulibaly to see increased burn off the Wizards' bench.

Beekman is set for an extended absence, with his re-evaluation timeline suggesting he could remain sidelined beyond the initial three-week window. The injury further limits Washington's backcourt depth, though Beekman's absence is unlikely to have a significant impact on standard fantasy leagues.
